We have carbon NMR shifts list. Need number of methyl (CH3) groups. Methyl carbons typically appear around 10-30 ppm for aliphatic methyls, maybe 14-30. In list we have low-field shifts: 24.56, 19.40, 16.60. Also maybe 34.00, 39.20, 41.00, 57.20 are other carbons (CH2, CH, etc). So likely three methyl groups. Need confirm if any other methyl like aromatic methyl (like toluene) appears ~20 ppm. Those three low shifts likely methyls. So answer 3.

Check if any other methyl could be at 57.20 (maybe O-CH3). But O-CH3 appears ~55 ppm. Could be a methoxy group (CH3 attached to O). That's also a methyl. So we might have 4 methyl groups: three aliphatic (16.6,19.4,24.56) and one methoxy (57.20). The question: "How many methyl (CH3) groups are present in the sample's molecule?" includes any CH3 regardless of environment. So count all carbon signals corresponding to CH3. Need to identify which carbons are CH3. We need more info maybe from proton NMR to differentiate. Could use proton NMR to see number of methyl proton signals. Let's get proton NMR.
